html:
The highest law of Kazakhstan, adopted by a referendum on 15 March 2026 and in force from 1 July 2026. It replaced the constitution of 1995.

The 1995 text had been written for Nursultan Nazarbayev and gave the president very wide powers. After the deadly unrest of January 2022, President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev began a series of changes meant to show a break with his predecessor. In his 2025 address he proposed reforms of parliament, first to be voted on in 2027. The vote was brought forward, and the reforms grew into a new constitution.

It is too early to judge how far the new law will change who holds power. Its adoption is the latest step in a long effort by the post Soviet state to remake its institutions while keeping control from the top.
sum: The highest law of Kazakhstan, adopted by a referendum on 15 March 2026 and in force from 1 July 2026. It replaced the constitution of 1995.
